problem: Digital-agent VLMs lack physical grounding (spatial geometry, action consequences, execution feedback), while existing embodied VLMs offer limited multi-turn agent reasoning, skill/tool invocation, execution monitoring and error diagnosis; the two are usually built separately or cascaded.
motivation: Physical AI needs both embodied cognition (spatial/temporal/feedback modeling) and agent abilities (long-horizon planning, tool/skill use, reflection) in one closed perception-reasoning-action-verification-replanning loop. Naively mixing heterogeneous RL objectives hurts domain capabilities, and edge deployment demands low latency.
key_idea: Build a single VLM by injecting embodied capability via SFT into a Qwen3.5 agent base, training separate embodied and agent expert RL policies, then merging them via multi-teacher on-policy distillation into an embodied-anchored student, plus edge-side token compression and W4A8 quantization.
insight: Specializing experts first (asymmetric initialization: agent from base, embodied from SFT checkpoint) and reconciling them afterwards via on-policy reverse-KL distillation lets one model keep both physical grounding and general agent/reasoning ability. Training-free Max-Min token selection retains 96.7% (4B) / 98.2% (35B) of the uncompressed score, and W4A8 costs <1%, so edge deployment is cheap in accuracy. No ablation of the training stages is reported, so the evidence for the pipeline is only the benchmark comparisons.
method: Data: open-source plus self-built data for physical understanding, task planning, error diagnosis/recovery (including perturbation-injected recovery trajectories from VLA rollouts), autonomous driving, and in-house R2R/RxR navigation dialogues (forward 25/50/75 cm, turn 15/30/45° for R2R and 30/60/90° for RxR; 1 or up to 3 actions per turn), plus multimodal agent/tool-use tasks
Embodied Capability Injection: two SFT stages (foundation SFT for physical grounding, reasoning SFT for condition/action/state-change/verification), giving pi_inj
Capability-Unit RL: GRPO group-normalized advantages with GSPO sequence-level ratio clipping, with task-specific rewards (exact, geometric, verifier/partial credit)
Environment-Loop RL: multi-turn rollouts in isolated sandboxes/simulators from reproducible snapshots, environment-coupled evaluators, failures kept in trajectories
Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation: student initialized from embodied expert, reverse KL to agent and embodied teachers on student rollouts with domain-dependent weights, no routing at inference
Edge deployment: training-free greedy Max-Min diversity visual token selection (4096→3328 tokens), W4A8 quantization, compiler/runtime co-design on Li Auto M100 NPU (prefill 400 ms→188 ms)

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-series native multimodal agent model (fine-tuned; 4B and 35B-A3B MoE variants)
setting.training_data: Open-source and self-produced embodied data (physical understanding, planning, error recovery), driving datasets, in-house R2R/RxR navigation dialogues, and agent tool-use tasks; scale not stated
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB frames (one new frame per turn for navigation), multi-view images/video
setting.action_space: Discrete high-level text actions: forward 25/50/75 cm, turn 15/30/45° (R2R) or 30/60/90° (RxR), STOP; 1 or up to 3 actions per turn
setting.simulator: Habitat-style R2R/RxR continuous simulator (unspecified), plus simulated manipulation environments

numbers_note: Navigation table only compares against other general embodied VLMs (not specialized VLN methods). The paper does not say whether R2R/RxR are the CE versions; inferred from continuous-style actions. No ablations of training stages.
results: ME-VLM 35B-A3B averages 70.9 on 26 embodied benchmarks (vs 62.7 for PhysBrain 1.5-8B) and 72.5 on agent benchmarks (vs 62.9 for RynnBrain 1.1-9B). On R2R val-unseen it gets SR 45.8 and on RxR SR 42.6, far above the embodied-VLM baselines (best SR 5.3 and 8.3). The 4B model averages 63.4 and runs on M100 with prefill cut 400→188 ms.
limitations: Navigation comparison is only against general embodied VLMs that were not trained for navigation, and no comparison to dedicated VLN methods; no ablations of SFT/RL/MOPD stages
Trails RynnBrain on TAU2-Bench and ClawEval; 4B lags on tool use and some benchmarks (marked abnormal results on MindCube, RoboBench-Error)
Training data scale and details are not disclosed; real-world and simulation results are qualitative only
